result.title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations
result.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used for expensive black-box optimization, yet observation noise makes each evaluation less informative and slows posterior learning. Standard BO learns from costly outcomes gathered during optimization. In many applications, however, low-cost auxiliary data are available beforehand. We introduce Auxiliary-Informed Gaussian Process Bandit (AI-GPB), a variance-reduction method that combines an offline estimate of the auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. Notably, it exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. We establish finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees, including explicit cumulative and simple regret rates for Matérn kernels. Numerical experiments across continuous BO benchmarks with varied landscapes and dimensions show consistent reductions in cumulative and simple regret relative to vanilla GP-UCB, even when within-pair correlation is moderate and the auxiliary mean is estimated from noisy offline data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AI-GPB：在 Gaussian Process Bandit 中把离线估计的辅助均值与从配对在线观测学到的修正系数结合，实现后验方差缩减，并给出置信界与 regret 率。
AI.relevance_reason: 廉价辅助观测加配对误差相关性以降低不确定性、指导探索与停止，可能与 LVR 中「用低成本视觉证据筛选支撑 latent 状态更新与停止决策」的思路有概念联系，可供核查。
